items.title: 63476_Jimmie Crawford oral history interview
items.q: my wife was working with a fellow by the name of Ralph Cooper

ctx.x: So I -- or we rather -- we took it upon ourselves to go around trying to look on the streets and find a penny so we could buy a penny's worth of peanuts and drink some water behind it and then you're full. Well, that's what I did, tried to find me some pennies, insert in those salted peanut machines they had in those days, drink some water behind it. Nobody gave me nothing.

I know they didn't give me anything. Lunsford starved, himself. And my wife was working with a fellow by the name of Ralph Cooper, who used to take shows on the road, playing the colored theaters and whatnot and clubs, and, well, Ralph had a little bit more incentive about him at that time. He would go in a town, and he would go and make arrangements with the owner of some restaurant where his employees or his dancing chorus line and fellows and acts and et cetera, they would go in and eat and then sign their…
